findings.issue: The step titles are now bold, which fixes part of the earlier finding, but the steps still have no numbers and are set as a two-column table ruled in solid black, while process-1 on the same page numbers its steps 01–05 in blue over light hairlines, so the page shows two step styles.
findings.reference: The competitor's numbered-steps module sets each step with a blue 01–03 numeral and a bold title over light rules, which is the style process-1 already follows.
findings.fix: In the shared steps companion of the process module, add the accent decimal-leading-zero numeral and the light rule (text colour at about 18%) that .block--process .point-list__items[data-numbered] uses, in place of the black row borders.

findings.issue: Same as overview-steps: 'Sign off sample and specs' to 'Bulk production' are set as an unnumbered table ruled in black, unlike the numbered blue steps of process-1 that follow it.
findings.reference: The competitor numbers its steps 01–03 in blue, with a bold title, over thin light rules.
findings.fix: Same component fix as overview-steps: accent numerals and light rules in the steps companion.

findings.issue: This was raised before and the current shots still show it: on phones an empty band of about 50px separates the caption 'How a typical order runs' from its first step, so the caption looks cut off from the list. m8-steps has the same gap under 'From sign-off to bulk production'.
findings.reference: The competitor's step lists follow their heading at the normal gap between a heading and its content.
findings.fix: In the single-column layout of the steps companion, replace the side-by-side row gap with the gap used between a heading and its content.

findings.issue: This was raised before and is still there: m3 'Stock Styles & Wholesale Buying' and m6 'Pricing & Quotes' are neighbouring check lists, and both set their items as a list beside the heading, so the page repeats one arrangement twice in a row.
findings.reference: Site rule: when two neighbouring sections are rows of short items, the template sets only one of them as a list beside its heading.
findings.fix: Have the template give m6 (or m3) the other iconList arrangement, items in columns under the heading as iconList-1 shows, when two iconList sections are neighbours.

findings.issue: This block has no heading of its own and continues m11 after proof-5 and proof-6, yet its first paragraph ('We measure your packed cartons…') still takes the larger lead size, so one paragraph in the middle of the section grows for no reason. Mobile shows the same.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps one body size through all the paragraphs of a text section.
findings.fix: Apply the lead style (.text-flow__lead) only to the first paragraph under a section heading, never to the first paragraph of a block without a heading that continues a section.

findings.issue: The fee chart still draws three identical full-width bars (Sample fee, Design fee and Courier delivery, all $50), which compares nothing, and the two timing bars float on tracks with no axis or scale.
findings.reference: The competitor shows figures only where they add information.
findings.fix: Have Site Factory give these facts as a short stats row or list (three $50 fees; 10–15 and 5–7 days) instead of bar charts of equal values.

findings.issue: The lone link is now sized to its own width, but the heading 'Related products and services' still sits over a single link to 'Case Studies', which is neither a product nor a service. The heading is also the only one on the page in sentence case.
findings.fix: Have Site Factory link related product or solution pages here, or retitle the section in Title Case to match its link.

findings.issue: On phones the wide CTA photo is cropped to a narrow card that puts the woman's face directly behind the heading 'Send Us Your Enquiry'. The overlay keeps the text readable, but heading and face collide.
findings.reference: The competitor sets text over photos only where the photo leaves an empty area for it.
findings.fix: Let the CTA image band take a separate portrait crop on phones, with the subject below or beside the copy area; moving the crop of the wide photo cannot clear the full-width copy.
